label: TP
reason: The CodeQL alert correctly identifies two XSS paths: (1) Cookie name derived from user-supplied HTTP header ('BenchmarkTest00297') flows directly into the response writer via toString() without HTML encoding, allowing script injection in the cookie name attribute. (2) User-supplied header value flows directly into the response writer via getValue() without HTML encoding, allowing script injection in the cookie value attribute. Both sinks are direct concatenations into HTML attributes/content without any neutralization.

evidence.note: Cookie name (from user header) and value (from user header) are concatenated into response.getWriter() without HTML encoding, enabling XSS.
Insecure randomness source identified by CodeQL (Random.nextGaussian()), which is also a genuine weakness though distinct from the XSS findings.
